root_idea.summary: A basic idea of variegation: colors or appearances differing from one another, producing spots, patches, or other forms of visible contrast.
root_idea.development: The root extends from contrasting coloration to distinct plots of land, patchy distribution, scattered rainfall, and figurative descriptions of people, events, and conditions marked by irregularity or difference.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun normalized as the classical citation form بُقْعَةٌ.

senses.definition: A distinct spot, plot, or portion of ground or place, set apart from what adjoins it.
senses.usage_conditions: In the sole Quran occurrence, 28:30, it denotes a specified place or spot. The lexical notion is a distinct portion or location rather than a general expanse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird or dog, to be black-and-white, variegated, or pied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to animals whose coloration is mixed or party-coloured.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become wetted or marked in scattered spots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a body affected by sprinkled water, with some portions wetted and others not.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away or disappear so that one's trace is lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially in the negative expression meaning “I do not know where he went.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a calamity or misfortune to befall people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal construction with a calamity as subject and the affected people as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be assailed with foul speech, calumny, slander, or false accusation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the passive construction بُقِعَ بِقَبِيحٍ and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mark, wet, or affect something in scattered spots, leaving portions distinct from others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of a dyer, leaving parts of cloth undyed; of a person, sprinkling water on a garment; and of rain, falling only in scattered places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away quickly or run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived verbal use denoting rapid departure or movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's color to change because of grief or sorrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's altered complexion or color under emotional distress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where water remains and stagnates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The place is characterized as not being a usual watering place for people or animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spot or small portion of a surface that differs from what surrounds it, including an undyed or water-retaining patch in cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a surface-level extension of the notion of visible difference and is distinct from the land-plot sense used in the Quran.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have a favorable station or standing with a ruler or commander.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for one's position in a person's favor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land containing separated patches of vegetation or bare areas.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description may refer to vegetation occurring in patches or to bare places produced by locusts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Discolorations left on the body when dust and sweat dry or whiten upon the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiom خُرْءُ بَقَاعِ and related expressions for visible marks on the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place containing the roots or remnants of trees of various kinds, or a spacious tract containing trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote a wooded or formerly wooded open place, as in بَقِيعُ الغَرْقَدِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cautious, wary, and cunning bird that avoids frequented watering places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bird drinks from stagnant or secluded water because it fears being caught.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is highly cunning, perceptive, experienced, and difficult to deceive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the wary bird; it may also describe someone skilful or quick in intellect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune that befalls a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative noun for a harmful event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Piebald or parti-coloured, especially black-and-white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied particularly to a crow or similar bird, and also to a dog; the feminine is بَقْعَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, evil, wicked, mischievous, or ill-omened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the traditional association of the pied crow with bad or ominous qualities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leprous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended adjectival use recorded as a distinct Classical meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People of mixed or contrasting coloring, especially a term applied to the servants or slaves of Syria.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained through mixtures of whiteness, redness, yellowness, or blackness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waterers whose bodies have become wet in scattered places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural usage referring to people whose bodies show irregular wet patches from carrying or drawing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People wearing patched garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes their poor or degraded condition through the contrasting patches of their clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels having white humps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive plural construction for contrasting coloration on the humps.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained by the mirage's varying or changing hues.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land containing or diversified with small pebbles and stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of stony, pebbly ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A barren or irregularly productive year, including a year whose rain falls only in scattered areas or is scant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description can emphasize barrenness, a mixture of fruitful and barren areas, patchy rainfall, or little rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the legs wetted in some places, so that those places differ in color from the rest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial description of irregularly wet legs or similar surfaces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man whose abundant speech wanders without a clear beginning or end.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Classical description of rambling or directionless talk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To swear an oath to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare attested verbal usage distinct from the color and patch meanings.

cautions: Several related forms are homographic in undiacritized writing; the vocalization and derived form distinguish the Quranic بُقْعَةٌ from forms such as بَقْعَةٌ, بَقِيعٌ, and أَبْقَعُ.
